Led by partners India Doris (formerly of two-Michelin-starred SAGA) and Alex Pfaffenbach (Eleven Madison Park, Quality Branded), the space pairs a nostalgia-driven cocktail program with Caribbean-influenced small plates and elevated sandwiches.

I tried not to panic realizing that I was going to miss the last 2 ferries that would get me to my gig ahead of time. My dear friend/ coworker Mario "The Fix" was riding along with me as we had just completed a task in Syosset L.I. 
He knew I was in a time crunch and did such an exceptional deed and offered to stay and wait on the subway platform with my semi-heavy hand truck loaded with my bowls, gongs, and c stand while I dashed back uptown to my whip. I thought that was the sweetest most clutch gesture that could have arrived at the moment. I saved time, anxiety and energy not having to lug that stuff up and down multiple staircases, I was back to him within 25 N.Y. minutes, (that's fast) and in the process, I contacted the contact and gave them an update on my predicament and he told me no worries, we'll just let the client know it's a delayed start and he would be there to pick me up from the ferry. 

Further relief was provided when my friend decided to accompany me to the ferry and carry my shoulder bags and assist me up the steps. I was so moved, I had to treat him to a fat lunch at Sophie's. All said and done the sound bath only started 15 minutes behind and  I managed to maintain my composure all the while which resulted in a very sweetened 1 hr session. That's all I could ask for. 🫶🏽

caption:
Our new Straight Empire Rye is more than just a new release, it’s a permanent addition to our signature collection, and a tribute to New York’s rich rye heritage. 

Crafted from NY grain and distilled in Brooklyn, this is our answer to what rye should taste like in the Empire State: distinctive and bold.

Empire Rye is a whiskey standard established by a group of New York distillers to revive the state’s pre-Prohibition rye tradition. To qualify, the whiskey must be made from at least 75% New York–grown rye, mashed, fermented, distilled, and aged entirely in-state, and aged for a minimum of two years in new charred oak barrels. Kings County Distillery is proud to be one of the originating distilleries behind the Empire Rye designation. 

Thank you so much for all of the online orders and to everyone who braved the weather and made our release party a wild success last week!  We appreciate all of your support— without you all we couldn’t embark on this ambitious project to bring rye distilling back to our state. 

Available now online, onsite, and rolling out to the best retailers in the next days and weeks. Ask for it wherever Kings County is sold.

This was my first time trying PopUp Bagels and the thing everyone talks about is real. That crispy, shiny outside to chewy pull to soft interior combo is the whole point.

When we were in New York, we were literally just hunting for a good bagel and ended up here. It was packed, still super popular, and it totally lived up to the hype texture wise.

We also tried Leon’s Bagels around the same time, which was great too. It honestly highlighted how different NYC bagels hit compared to LA. Different chew, different vibe, different expectations.

PopUp feels very intentional. Not a classic deli bagel. More like a hot, fresh bagel built for the smear.

I get why people love them. Not saying it replaces every classic bagel, but for texture alone, I’m in 💯.

Трудно поверить, что этот просторный, великолепный мексиканский ресторан от создателей Bad Roman был парковкой 
Но Limusina сохранила немного брутальности: на бетонных колоннах вручную нарисованы изящные цветы, а красочные занавески из сетки выполнены в стиле омбре, напоминающем коктейль «текила-санрайз».
Однако меню — это сплошной блеск, и почти все блюда имеют сладковатый (или немного солоноватый) вкус. 
Фондю из сыра с кунжутом, фламбированное прямо за столом, немного напоминает запеченный бри с джемом. Хрустящая кесадилья с черным трюфелем и гуавовым джемом — неплохая, но очень похожа на бутерброд с арахисовым маслом и джемом.
Закажите ярко-зеленый гуакамоле, хорошо прожаренный мексиканский рис тахдиг или, может быть, очень сытные черные бобы алиго. И обязательно попробуйте Flaca — маргариту с красным апельсином и острым перцем серрано. 
Она названа в честь высокого, тонкого бокала, в котором подается, и который после первого же бокала будет все труднее не опрокинуть.❤️❤️❤️

Being a content creator is such a vulnerable thing — it requires you to take up space.

You show up online as your authentic self. Sometimes it feels like you’re talking into a void. You’ve got meetings with your marketing, operations, and creative team — the gag is, you are the team. All of it. And it can feel lonely.

You wonder if what you create is helping someone, or if it’s inspiring someone else to bet on themselves.

Thank you to @flodesk for this incredible night of inspiration and for reminding me that the world needs what I’ve got.

This job requires you to fully bet on yourself — and take up space doing it.

Over the past few weeks, I’ve been lucky to attend some amazing events, but the one with Flodesk was by far one of the most memorable. I was in a room full of entrepreneurs who face the same challenges and know the power of an email marketing platform that helps us reach our communities and amplify our work.

Thanks to @williamadwinphotography for capturing these moments, because I def talk with my hands. 🤣

🎥 Our typical on set process looks like this:

-Nick and I work together on lighting & colors, while Zach adjusts camera settings to make sure the lighting reads

-The dancer does a walk-through to highlight any major direction & level changes for Zach to know before filming. Then, after ONE walk-through, we film. We watch playback and work together on any adjustments needed to better highlight the movement (if any jump out at us). Then we all run it again!

-Repeat!

That said, we have a lot of “1-take Wonders” here at TDF, so I schedule only FIFTEEN minutes for ALL of this per piece 👀 (thirty minutes for small group shots). It’s a well-oiled machine at this point 🔥

Every five years, my husband and I say…
“We have to meet each other again.”
Because we are always becoming. Always evolving.
And today, I feel it’s time to reintroduce myself, not because I’ve changed, but because I’ve grown deeper into who I’ve always been.
I am Yesenia Maria Ramdass 😊
Founder, Owner, Chef…
But before all of that, I’m a mother, a daughter, a wife.
The sixth of 7 children.
100% Dominicana 🇩🇴born and raised in Washington Heights.
A first generation dreamer raised on Bachata and merengue.
A vegetarian of 13 years, A vegan of 7 years, a storyteller through food. 
And the hands behind HAAM 🌱
A space born from grief 🦋💙 from purpose, from the fire of reinvention.
This journey started with me writing blogs, to doing how to YouTube videos, then to becoming a mom and cooking for my babies all after losing my mother to cancer 😢
Pouring my heartbreak into healing meals, trying to find a way to not let her death be in vain.
Then a tent.
Then a table.
Then strangers lining up for food that tasted like home.
I had no restaurant experience.
Only heart ❤️ 
But heart led me here.
To a brick and mortar built on love, loss, legacy, and plantanos.
To honoring my mother’s spirit through every dish.
To creating a space where my community can feel seen, nourished, and proud.
So whether you’ve known me from the beginning,
Or you’re meeting me for the first time
This is me.
This is HAAM.
THANK YOU FOR BEING HERE ❤️

A common question we see from Excel power users 👇
 “Can I create dependent dropdowns in monday.com like Excel?”
Here’s the expert answer:
❌ NOT THAT:
 Trying to recreate true Excel-style dynamic dropdowns.
 monday.com doesn’t currently support dropdown options that change dynamically based on another column’s value, and forcing it leads to messy data and fragile setups.
✅ DO THIS (the expert approach):
 Design around the platform using proven patterns:
• Use a category column (Fruits / Vegetables)
 • Use automations to clear or reset the second column when the category changes
 • Or split into separate columns (Fruit Type / Vegetable Type) and show or hide them with automations
 • If data is collected via Forms, use conditional logic to show the correct dropdown automatically
The result?
 ✔ Clean data
 ✔ Fewer mistakes
 ✔ A system that scales instead of breaking

We’ve been MIA during our hiatus, but this can’t wait. Our friends and mentors from @volaband are in a crisis - their storage facility just caught on fire, taking everything with it. Luckily, everyone’s safe, but the loss is immense, and as musicians ourselves, we know how devastating this must be.

The guys from VOLA are some of the kindest and most genuine people we’ve ever met. As a band whose music doesn’t fit neatly into any single box, we’ve learned that while being a bit culturally specific might be our strength in a city like New York, it sometimes makes people in the industry unsure where we belong. VOLA never treated that as a liability and instead understood what we were trying to build and supported us wholeheartedly. They welcomed us, trusted the music, and handpicked us to share a stage with them this September in Gramercy Theatre. That day, we said to them again and again - and will say it again this time - that this meant so much to us, so much more than they probably realize.

To those who know us, you know how much gratitude we carry with us. We don’t take for granted anyone who offered a hand when we needed it most, and we’ll always have your back. That’s the doctrine of being a silkpunk. 

Please help out if you can via the link or in our story: https://gofund.me/d45fbe3f4
